name: Battery Status API and drain inference
plain: Reads battery level, charging state and time estimates in Chromium browsers.
meaning: Level and discharge time can short-term link visits across sites. Remaining time infers device load. Removed from Firefox and never added to Safari because of the tracking risk.

web.api: navigator.getBattery(); BatteryManager level, charging, chargingTime, dischargingTime

limits.headline: Can see your battery level and charging state in Chromium browsers
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, or when a page checks power use
can: Check your battery level and if you are charging
Check how long until it is full or empty
Use short lived numbers to link two visits close together
cannot: Get battery info in Firefox, which removed it, or in Safari, which never added it
Know who you are by itself
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet allow it. Firefox removed it and Safari never added it because of tracking worries.

story.what_it_is: A page reads your battery level, whether you are charging and time left. Only some browsers allow it.

marketing.name: Battery Status API
marketing.pitch: Lets a page see the device's battery level and charging state, so it can save power when low.

story.for_you: You get no prompt. A page might switch to a lighter mode or pause fancy effects when your battery is low. Researchers showed it could be used to track people, so Firefox and Safari left it out.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to save power and avoid draining a phone in the middle of a game or video. It also works as a small device signal, which is why privacy minded browsers removed it.

use_cases.example: A browser game lowers the frame rate and effects when you are under 20 percent battery.
A streaming site picks a lower resolution on low battery to let you finish the movie.
A video call tool turns off background blur when your laptop is unplugged and low.
A web editor saves your work sooner when battery is about to die.
A tracker combines battery level and time to charge as a short lived device ID.
Privacy researchers warned that a shop could change prices for people with a low battery, which is one reason the feature was removed.
A web workout player skips heavy animations on a phone that is almost out of power.

technical_bounds: Cannot read battery on iOS or Firefox
Can't see battery health, only level

value.abuse: Short-term device linking (Olejnik 2015), retail price discrimination claims

history.change: Battery API removed over privacy concerns
Restricted to secure contexts and permissions policy battery

refs.label: Olejnik et al., The Leaking Battery (2015)
